entities.name: Ḥumaydī, ʻAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
ʻAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr al-Ḥumaydī (died 834 CE) emerged as a pivotal figure in the early development of Islamic jurisprudence, specifically within the nascent Shafi'i school of thought, during the Abbasid Caliphate. Operating primarily from the intellectual hubs of Mecca and Baghdad, al-Ḥumaydī was not merely a student but a direct transmitter and consolidator of the teachings of Imam al-Shafi'i, thereby playing a critical role in formalizing and disseminating one of Sunni Islam's four major legal traditions across the Arabian Peninsula and beyond. His direct tutelage under al-Shafi'i positioned him as an authoritative link to the school's founder, granting his compilations immense credibility and enduring influence in the subsequent centuries of Islamic legal scholarship.

Al-Ḥumaydī's most enduring contribution is his monumental work, *Al-Musnad*, a collection of Hadith (prophetic traditions) organized by the Companion from whom the Hadith was narrated, rather than by subject matter. This methodological choice distinguished it from later thematic Hadith collections and provided a crucial resource for understanding the early transmission chains of Islamic law. He meticulously recorded and transmitted the legal opinions (*fatāwā*) and jurisprudential methods (*usūl al-fiqh*) of al-Shafi'i, often directly from his master's *majlis* (study circle) in Mecca and later in Egypt. As the 'Shaykh of al-Haram' in Mecca, he held significant religious authority, attracting numerous students and effectively serving as a primary conduit for the propagation of Shafi'i thought to the wider Islamic world.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Al-Ḥumaydī's meticulous Hadith collection and direct transmission of Imam al-Shafi'i's teachings were crucial for formalizing and disseminating one of Sunni Islam's four major legal traditions, profoundly shaping Islamic law and education for over a millennium. His work influenced subsequent canonical Hadith compilers and solidified the intellectual foundation of the Shafi'i madhhab.
